claims.text: FAA's 2023 Zipline Exemption 19111B distinguishes operation-specific relief from authorization of the DAA system itself.
claims.scope: US civil UAS; Zipline Exemption 19111B; historical 2023 decision
claims.challenge: Read the exact later amendment, each condition and any separate DAA-system approval before describing current authority or a particular system configuration.

claims.text: Zipline's 2024 exemption amendment requires an Area of Operations plan to include a safety case for DAA expansion and an airspace analysis below 500 feet.
claims.scope: US civil UAS; Zipline Exemption 19111C; historical 2024 decision
claims.challenge: This is a condition in a specific dated decision; do not convert it into a universal FAA learned-autonomy assurance requirement.

claims.text: TSO-C211a sets minimum performance standards for DAA equipment manufacturer applications and states that installation requires separate approval.
claims.scope: US civil aviation DAA equipment; TSO-C211a effective 2026-02-26
claims.challenge: Do not infer that an article is authorized, installed, operationally approved, or capable in a particular ODD merely because this TSO exists.

claims.text: On September 15, 2026, the public TxDMV lookup listed Tesla Robotaxi, LLC as Authorized from May 14, 2026 and showed 2026 Tesla Cybercab entries in its vehicle table.
claims.challenge: Recheck the live record before publication and preserve the date. Texas operating authorization does not establish federal compliance, passenger-service scope, or the safety of the learned driving system.

claims.text: FAA Exemption 19031B records that Amazon Prime Air's requested relief to remove visual observers when onboard DAA is employed remained under review and would be addressed separately.
claims.scope: US civil UAS; Amazon Prime Air Exemption 19031B; historical 2023 decision
claims.challenge: Find the later FAA disposition before stating whether Amazon received that relief or whether its scope resembles Zipline's authorization.
